claude.sample_unit: pathologists scoring 35 biopsy regions of interest

links.outcome: Pathologist interobserver agreement at PD-L1 CPS ≥5 with vs without AI assistance
links.effect: Fleiss' kappa rose from 0.52 (manual) to 0.76 (AI-assisted), p<0.01; agreement among all 11 pathologists 43% vs 69%; any two 77% vs 91%.
links.quote: Agreement among pathologists by Fleiss’ Kappa showed overall improved agreement from 0.52 (0.40–0.65) with manual scoring on day 1 to 0.76 (0.62-0.87) with AI-assisted scoring on day 2 with statistical significance ( p < 0.01, Bootstrapping of differences) (Fig. 3 c).

links.outcome: AI performance as used by pathologists in workflow (manual vs AI-assisted scoring agreement and positive calls)
links.effect: AI assistance increased ICC (e.g., total tumor cells 0.38 to 0.90) and positive CPS≥5 cases from 15 to 26 (31% increase).
links.quote: Pathologists identified 15 cases as PD-L1 CPS ≥ 5 positive with manual scoring on day 1 compared to 26 cases as PD-L1 CPS ≥ 5 positive by AI-assisted scoring on day 2, corresponding to a 31% increase of positive cases found when using AI-assistance.

links.outcome: AI agreement with reference consensus on independent held-out test set of 55 cases from 3 labs
links.effect: Fine-tuned model agreement 96.4% (95% CI 88.6-100) vs 81.8% for foundation model; kappa 0.91 vs 0.62; further validated on 97 independent biopsies.
links.quote: Data for AI development, both for pretraining and finetuning, did not overlap with the study data.

openai.sample_unit: ROIs/biopsy cases in ARM experiment, rated by 11 pathologists
models_evaluated: ARM-AI system with Gastric PD-L1 CPS AI Model

links.effect: Agreement improved from 81.8% before Gastric Cell Atlas decision rules to 96.4% after.
links.quote: Left, agreement of Gastric PD-L1 CPS AI Model against reference consensus score before Gastric Cell Atlas decision rules (81.8%) and after (96.4%).

Compared to the original IHC foundation model, the finetuned Gastric PD-L1 CPS AI Model showed improved concordance against the reference consensus increasing agreement from 81.8% (95% CI, 68.6%, 94.3%) to 96.4% (95% CI, 88.6%, 100%) ( p < 0.05, McNemar’s test) and Cohen’s Kappa κ from 0.62 (95% CI, 0.36, 0.86) to 0.91 (95% CI, 0.71, 1.0) ( p < 0.05, Bootstrapping) (Fig. 1c ).

links.effect: At CPS ≥5, AI-pathologist κ=0.46 (95% CI, 0.37, 0.54) vs pathologist-pathologist κ=0.39 (95% CI, 0.29, 0.48); p < 0.05.
links.quote: At a PD-L1 CPS ≥ 5 cut-off, the concordance between PD-L1 AI scores and pathologists’ manual scores was higher (Cohen’s κ = 0.46; 95% CI, 0.37, 0.54) than the average concordance among pathologists’ manual scores (Cohen’s κ = 0.39; 95% CI, 0.29, 0.48) with statistical significance ( p < 0.05, Bootstrapping) as well as higher than for the original IHC foundation model ( p < 0.001, Bootstrapping).

Using difficult to interpret regions on gastroesophageal biopsies, we show that AI-assistance improved case agreement between any 2 pathologists by 14% (agreement on 77% vs 91%) and among 11 pathologists by 26% (agreement on 43% vs 69%).

links.effect: Fleiss’ κ improved from 0.52 (0.40–0.65) manual to 0.76 (0.62-0.87) AI-assisted; p < 0.01.
links.quote: Agreement among pathologists by Fleiss’ Kappa showed overall improved agreement from 0.52 (0.40–0.65) with manual scoring on day 1 to 0.76 (0.62-0.87) with AI-assisted scoring on day 2 with statistical significance ( p < 0.01, Bootstrapping of differences) (Fig. 3 c).

links.outcome: Model concordance with reference consensus score
links.effect: Agreement increased from 81.8% to 96.4% (p < 0.05) and Cohen's kappa from 0.62 to 0.91 (p < 0.05)
links.quote: Compared to the original IHC foundation model, the finetuned Gastric PD-L1 CPS AI Model showed improved concordance against the reference consensus increasing agreement from 81.8% (95% CI, 68.6%, 94.3%) to 96.4% (95% CI, 88.6%, 100%) ( p < 0.05, McNemar’s test) and Cohen’s Kappa κ from 0.62 (95% CI, 0.36, 0.86) to 0.91 (95% CI, 0.71, 1.0) ( p < 0.05, Bootstrapping) (Fig. 1c ).
